title: You've been told you have 5 senses. Try 33 👃
description:
Close your eyes and touch your nose: you just used a sense that's not on the school list. Proprioception (muscle sensors that map your body), balance (fluid in three loops in your inner ear), heat, cold, pain, your heartbeat and hunger... Depending on how you split them, scientists count 22 to 33 senses, not Aristotle's five.

Sources: Charles Spence (Oxford Crossmodal Research Lab) via VICE; BBC Science Focus (Lisa Feldman Barrett); 'Human senses and sensors from Aristotle to the present', Frontiers in Neurology 2024.
tags: how many senses do humans have

meta.topic: how many senses you really have: proprioception (nose test), balance (inner-ear fluid loops), heat/cold/pain, heartbeat/hunger; 22-33 by scientists' counts vs Aristotle's 5
meta.idea_source: backlog (ideas.md "You've been told: we have 5 senses", the review's hook test) + viral-shaped (a school 'fact' overturned with a test you do on yourself) + unique angle (do-it-now nose test)
meta.experiment: 'you've been told X' hook test (review 2026-11-15), 1 of 2

humour.trend: Tony Stark head-turn format (the sideways 'I noticed that' glance, trending early Nov 2026) as a side-eye cut-away: 'my stomach when chips open two rooms away'

claims.claim: the five-sense list goes back to Aristotle
scientists count roughly 22 to 33 senses depending on how they are split (Charles Spence, Oxford)
proprioception: receptors in muscles, tendons and joints tell the brain where the limbs are
balance: fluid in the three semicircular canals of the inner ear senses rotation and keeps moving after you stop spinning
separate receptors for temperature and pain; interoception senses heartbeat and hunger

speaker: ved
